<ConflictType>Complementary information — The documents provide different aspects of the legal smoking age: federal law, state variations, historical context, and possession vs. sales rules.

The query asks for the age to smoke, which can refer to the legal age to purchase, possess, or smoke in public. The documents provide complementary facets: d3, d4, d6, d7, and d9 state the federal minimum sales age is 21 nationwide as of December 2019 [d3, d4, d6, d7, d9]. d1 and d8 note that states have set the age to 21, with d8 mentioning some state variations. d2 provides information on possession (no minimum age) and sales (18 in some contexts), and d5 discusses historical minimum ages of 18. These are not contradictory but address different dimensions (federal vs. state, sales vs. possession, current vs. historical).

The evidence collectively shows the primary answer is the federal minimum sales age of 21, with additional context on state alignment, possession rules, and historical baselines. The complementary information fits together to give a complete picture.

The federal minimum legal sales age for tobacco products in the United States is 21 years old, as established by federal law in December 2019 [d3, d4, d6, d7, d9]. This applies to all 50 states and the District of Columbia [d3, d8]. However, some documents note that state laws had previously set the age at 18 [d5] and that there is no minimum age to possess tobacco or smoke in public in some jurisdictions [d2]. The retrieved information is complementary, covering the federal standard, state-level variations, and distinctions between sales and possession.
